programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New goes through some of the keys he likes in his jig when targeting bass in the prespawn. New breaks down his jig trailer and why it's efficient and also explains an adjustment to his jig size that he used to never use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher gives his take on a few productive lures in the prespawn and how he balances their uses to be most effective while on the water. Should you use a Chatterbait where a jig could also work or vice versa he attacks this and more in this scenario.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Card
programme.desc: Brandon Card gives his thoughts on early season jerkbait fishing. Card gives scenarios when he will opt for a different cadence for his jerkbait rod length and line size.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Todd Auten
programme.desc: Todd Auten goes over three Chatterbait variations that have made the South Carolina pro successful with this technique. Whether it's color selection trailer options or getting the bait to ride high in the water column or fall fast Auten has his process. 1. White/CChartuese w/Zoom Shimmer Shad 2. Black/Blue w/Zoom ZCraw or Green Pumpkin Fluke 3. Firecraw w/Speed Craw

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyoya Fujita
programme.desc: Kyoya Fujita gives the specifics of his lures that helped him win at Toledo Bend. Fujita was using a technique called "mid-strolling" to get his Jackall Drift Fry and his Deps Sakamata Shad to the correct depth to target suspended bass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Trey McKinney
programme.desc: Lake Fork Champion Trey McKinney gives his lure arsenal as he adjusted daily to the changing fish for the second stop of the Elite Series season. Early in the event he used a jerkbait and jig head minnow combo but as the weather warm and conditions changed his baits adapted. Culminating on the final day were multiple baits contributed to his 130-15 tournament weight.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brad Whatley
programme.desc: Brad Whatley gives his strategy of covering water around the spawn when there is thicker cover present. Whatley winds his weighted swimbait around spawning areas and will trigger strikes or boils revealing where bass are positioned to catch on another tactic if necessary.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kenta Kimura
programme.desc: Kenta Kimura gives some suggestions to be better with the Megabass Magdraft swimbait. He changes the treble to his signature Ryugi quad-hook design for better hookups and he also adds a split ring to the line tie for increased head action and roll. Those two things are essential for Kimura along with finding the right speed on retrieve.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Hamner
programme.desc: Justin Hamner gives his strategy to catch key bass each day of competition and how he utilized multiple kinds of jerkbaits and mixed in a jig to catch the majority of his weight on Grand Lake in the 2024 Bassmaster Classic.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Bernie Schultz gives his three trusted lures when he is covering water to develop a pattern in the spring. He balances a spinnerbait swim jig and chatterbait when he approaches different types of cover.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Patrick
programme.desc: Kyle Patrick gives his approach for fishing for less pressured fish during the spawning months of the year. The fishing myth around the spawn is that bass have to go to the bank to do their yearly spawn when in reality fish can spawn much deeper and will take longer to do so.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Garrett
programme.desc: John Garrett runs down the three baits that were key for his win on the Harris Chain of Lakes. Garrett rotated between these techniques depending on how the fish were positioned and their aggressiveness on the shell bar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston goes over his two main lures for bed fishing at the St. Johns River en route to his first Elite Series victory. Johnston also explains his use of Perspective Mode when seeing bed fish in low visibility times.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Caleb Sumrall
programme.desc: Caleb Sumrall talks about one of the best ways to catch big bass. Sumrall strongly believes in a frog but when bass start shying away or missing it he downsizes instead of changing baits completely. When conditions change bass moods can vary and with that topwater becomes a high risk high reward situation and Sumrall will downsize to the keep the odds in his favor.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Seth Feider
programme.desc: Seth Feider goes through his wood jig and grass jig setup. He explains the differences in line tie and weed guard why he likes a short hook and his colors for flipping. Whether it's docks laydowns shoreline grass or submerged vegetation; Feider will often rely on a jig to get it done. His favorite size is a 5/8 ounce.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Patrick Walters
programme.desc: Elite Series Champion Patrick Walters gives the details of his approach at Lake Murray. Walters relied on a few baits throughout the week to win the event wire to wire. When fish were active and schooling Walters utilized a Zoom Super Fluke and a Rapala Jowler.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube walks us through one of his favorite techniques in tournaments and fun fishing. Dube gives his take on practicing with a Glide Bait and his strategy to convert followers into fish that will commit to biting.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New lays out one of his favorite topwater presentations the Buzz Toad. Pioneered by his good friend and fellow Elite Todd Auten New likes to use this bait to imitate multiple types of forage bass will eat in the post-spawn.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Crews
programme.desc: John Crews offers a different option for enticing schooling fish to bite when it gets tough and pressured in the summer. Using a Spy Bait can offer up another look that is great for casting and mimicking baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brock Mosley
programme.desc: Brock Mosley praises the most versatile lure in bass fishing the Yamamoto Senko. He shows how you can quickly switch from fishing the Senko weightless wacky rigged to adding a weight and changing the hook positioning for a Neko Rig. This lure will get fish to bite every day of the year depending on how you rig it.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cliff Prince
programme.desc: Cliff Prince dials us in on his 1/2 ounce Chatterbait setup that helped him win the Bassmaster Elite at Wheeler Lake. He also dishes the details on his magic spot and why he thinks the morning was incredible every day for him.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Cobb
programme.desc: Brandon Cobb gives his top picks for effective baits on lakes with blueback herring. Spotted bass and largemouth will get hyper focused on blueback herring when they exist on a body of water and Cobb knows these baits will work throughout the year and not a certain specific season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Taku Ito
programme.desc: Taku Ito goes through two key baits to his Bassmaster Elite Series victory at Smith Lake. From Neko Rigging a bluegill imitating bait to dropshotting a Magnum Fuzzy Dice he managed the biggest bass and bag to win.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Parks
programme.desc: Logan Parks discusses a strategy he employed at Wheeler during his first Top 10. Varying line size can help crankbaits run different depth and retrieved faster or slower. It's something he recommends during the summer months when schools are forming offshore or have been fished for frequently.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Latuso
programme.desc: Logan Latuso discusses a big key in the summer months...SHADE. This underrated aspect of the summer can get you some of the biggest bites of your day and it seemingly gets better as the day progresses. Take notes from Latuso and don't run your shade pattern too early to ensure some of your best success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Arey
programme.desc: Matt Arey talks about the importance of varying your retrieve with swimbaits over structure like brush piles. This is something that can be done with or without forward facing sonar as Arey describes the trial and error used prior to newer technology.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jake Whitaker
programme.desc: Jake Whitaker talks about the shallow bite windows that open up even with 100 degree days in the south. Whitaker leans on a topwater toad around any sort of cover that could hold fish. Anglers may get less bites in the heat of the summer but they can be the quality you need in a tournament.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Clifford Pirch
programme.desc: Clifford Pirch gives us a few ways to rig a drop shot if you're specifically targeting smallmouth and spotted bass. Threading his worm on weedless is his ideal setup but when fishing for smallmouth and spotted bass they tend to be more open water and less obstructions around. That's when Pirch will opt for a few other methods for fall rate and action.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Ed Laughran III
programme.desc: Lake Champlain Champion Ed Loughran runs through his jig setup that accounted for most of the fish throughout his tournament. He also leaned on a topwater in practice and on Championship Monday to catch smallmouth.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston gives a quick bait breakdown of a key lure that helped him win the 2024 Bassmaster Elite Series event at the St. Lawrence River. Johnston battled the waves out in Lake Ontario on the final two days of the event to secure a win his second of the season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jacob Foutz
programme.desc: Jacob Foutz walks us through his process of selecting sizes of jig heads when targeting bass in flooded timber. His sizes are as follows; 3/16 oz (5 to 10 feet) 1/4 oz (10 to 15 feet) 3/8 oz (20 feet and deeper). Foutz doesn't like getting any heavier than that if he can because of the leverage it gives fish to easily jump and throw the hook.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cody Huff
programme.desc: Cody Huff explores the benefits he's found when using various spoons during the late summer. He has dialed in his setups and doesn't experiment with multiple brands of spoons but rather uses the same spoons and changes sizes based on situation. From a magnum spoon to a compact jigging spoon Huff has found success on these from the Tennessee River to the Ozarks and many places in between.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey dishes out a few of his must-have baits for the early fall fishing season for Smallmouth bass. Downey who lives in Minnesota knows how incredible the bite can be this time of year before cold temps hit daily. Given the type of lake Downey has options for you in this video.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tyler Williams
programme.desc: Tyler Williams reveals the details to his 3/4 ounce jig he uses across the country. Upsizing his line can help slow the fall of his heavy jig along with pairing the jig with a big bulky trailer. Williams will use this jig around docks brush piles ledges and when targeting specific fish on his forward-facing sonar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: Greg Hackney gives some love to an often-forgotten lure for smallmouth fishing and that is the good ole fashioned tube. Hackney still appreciates what a tube brings to the table while fishing for smallmouth on competition days.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock talks about one of the most fun techniques and lures that is so effective in the Fall season. Covering water with a Berkley Choppo is essential and allows Shryock to burn through dead water in no time with this approach and it is a tournament winning formula.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt pulls 4 swim jigs out of his tackle box to showcase their effectiveness on different pieces of cover and depths. A simple trailer change can help Schmitt's swim jig stay shallow or go deeper. Schmitt gives the nuts and bolts to swim jig fishing his way and style.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Cox
programme.desc: John Cox gives a look at two of his favorite topwater lures and ones he trusts in the Fall. Whether it's around grass wood or rock both of these lures are on his front deck this time of year. Cox experimented with a longer frog rod this season and it helped him land a 3rd place finish at Wheeler Lake.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Lester
programme.desc: Brandon Lester gives us two key factors he relies on when choosing between a Jig and Texas Rig which is often a debate in the Fall fishing season. Profile and rate of fall depending on the seasonal conditions are considerations for the two-time BASS winner.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen runs down his three favorite colors for squarebill crankbaits in the fall. Another essential aspect to a squarebill that Lowen cherishes is a circuit board bill vs a plastic bill. It gives the crankbait the feel and characteristic of a balsa crankbait while maintaining the durability of a plastic crankbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Atkins
programme.desc: Justin Atkins sheds light on the flats. A vast area of consistent contour depths and also a place where baitfish and bass congregate as the season turns to cooler temperatures in the fall. This can be a great landing spot for bass as they get positioned to feed during this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson pulls out his favorite bait for the fall when the water temperatures are falling and in many situations the water level is falling too. When the bass start keying in on crawfish with cooling water J-Will knows its jig season. With living rubber skirted jigs Williamson fishes a 1/2 ounce or 3/4 ounce jig and never goes lighter than 1/2 ounce. He will also target brush early and as it continues to cool down will move to rock through the winter.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: One of the best structure fishermen in the world Brandon Palaniuk talks about isolated structure in the fall season. BP also gives a few bait suggestions including his handy dropshot.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin gives us his version of Thanksgiving turkey and fixings with this three-bait lineup this time of year. He has a bait for every level of the water column depending on how the fish are acting and where you're fishing this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes talks about the shallow nature of fish even when the temperatures are dropping across the country. The first feeling anglers have when the water temperatures drop is to fish deeper water but Cifuentes mentions how even in the Ozarks bass will hang out around shallow wood and rock still keyed in on a bigger meal that imitates dying baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Herren
programme.desc: Matt Herren goes through the process of fishing current seams on rivers with a spinnerbait. No matter time of year water current is a great place to find fish and target where bass are positioned and if you find the correct lineup it can be fast action. Herren recommends a 1/2-ounce to 3/4-ounce compact spinnerbait to avoid snags and hangups and control the bait despite the current pushing and washing the spinnerbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Alex Wetherell
programme.desc: Alex Wetherell discusses two soft plastics he uses around his home in Connecticut and down south when the calendar hits December. Balls of bait equal bass for Wetherell as they actively feed even when the water temperatures are cooler at the end of the year. Bass aren’t nearly as lethargic as we once believed years ago.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses fishing a jerkbait around Christmas time and how two of his baits act totally different. Christie breaks down how the Smithwick Rogue and Booyah Flash Point react different on the same cadence. Water temperatures in the 40's Christie opts for the Rogue. Meanwhile he sees positive results with the quick-working Flash Point with temperatures in the 50's and even 60's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Wes Logan
programme.desc: Wes Logan talks moving water and how he approaches it. Being from the Coosa River Logan is used to fishing moving water no matter the time of year and these three baits help him have good success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew relies on a jerkbait from late fall through the spawn whether using electronics or not. He keeps two color options: translucent for sunny or clear water and solid for cloudy or stained conditions.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt highlights how different SPRO Aruku Shad versions and hook sizes enhance performance based on season cover and action. He adjusts for fall rates with yo-yo or straight retrieves and downsizes when the bite is tough.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock relies on burning a crankbait over grass rock and stumps during late winter and pre-spawn. He ups his line size to keep the bait higher and uses a 7'4" rod for longer casts and ripping it free from grass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Robert Gee
programme.desc: Robert Gee reflects on his 2024 success with largemouth smallmouth and spotted bass noting that spots and smallmouth chase differently than largemouth requiring presentation adjustments. He shares his preferred head sizes go-to knot and a simple rod and reel setup most anglers can use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube discusses his use of a deep diving jerkbait to cover water depths from 4 feet out to 15 feet or so. Dube exclusively uses 10 to 12-pound line and will change his cadence from fast early in the retrieve to slower in the strike zone.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Emil Wagner
programme.desc: Emil Wagner sheds light on his favorite bait for winter fishing especially on spotted bass lakes like Lanier. With jig head minnows neko rigs and dropshots becoming popular everyone forgot about the shaky head.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin sets up the calendar for Florida's Spawn Cycle. Depending on weather spawn can start in south Florida as early as Thanksgiving week and extend through May of the next year. Martin gives his take on the difference of a lake like Okeechobee and the St. Johns River farther north.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen explains his two-pronged approach at the St. Johns River sticking to one area for four days using a black and blue swim jig and a flipping jig. He highlights his swim jig cadence and the importance of his flipping jig falling into hard cover

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: Brandon Palaniuk shares the three baits he used to win the Bassmaster Elite Series at Lake Okeechobee: a Megabass Kanata jerkbait and two Megabass crankbaits (Big M and a prototype). Fishing one spot aggressively led to some of the biggest strikes seen on Bassmaster LIVE.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock discusses the rising trend of using a swimbait in the prespawn as a substitute for commonly thrown baits with similar profiles. Fished around the same shallow cover it can trigger the big kicker bite tournament anglers seek.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson provides a solution to those tricky bass that are days from spawning and sit high in the water column. Not only does a jig provide great opportunities for good catches but a swimbait also entices those big females to commit.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Easton Fathergill
programme.desc: Easton Fothergill gives his daily adjustment to how fish were positioned each day of the Classic. From windy days to calm moments Fothergill kept adjusting his tackle to maximize efficiency.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey goes through what he would consider his spring selection for largemouth fishing. Spring means March and April in the south but can mean April May and June up north. Downey opts for a crankbait swim jig and two types of soft plastics when making the spring transition.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen goes through two baits he always has rigged up this time of year. A tube and a jig are staples in Lowen's boat and he explains how both get fished in conjunction with one another. There are a few variables like pegging his weight or letting it free flow and also line size in these situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher breaks down his single bait that produced a record winning margin and over 118 pounds of bass at the Pasquotank River. Flipping a Rapala CrushCity Bronco Bug to shallow roamers and spawning bass was his strategy. He utilized his forward facing sonar to pick out fish among the cover littered on the bottom.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: The Shad Spawn is a unique stage of the fishing season that bridges the gap from the bass spawn into the post spawn. Shad spawning around hard shallow cover gives bass a great opportunity to feed heavily in a short window of time. Not all places in the country feature a shad spawn but if threadfin are present in your lake a shad spawn is likely to happen. Low-light conditions early in the morning are helpful and baits like a spinnerbait imitate small shad perfectly to load the boat for Greg Hackney in a hurry.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Paul Marks
programme.desc: Paul Marks shows off his single bait that produced in two different situations depending on how he rigged it. The Zoom Fluke Stick in Natural Shad contributed almost all of his weight in his Elite victory at Lake Hartwell. His first approach was rigging it weightless to throw on shallow points where bass pushed blueback herring to feed in the morning then he switch to a shakey head in the afternoons.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses the tricky period immediately after bass leave the bed and are either guarding fry or recovering from the spawn. Here is how Christie opts to catch them.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tucker Smith
programme.desc: Tucker Smith talks about finding hard spots on Lake Fork with his side imaging throughout practice and then using his forward facing sonar to execute and catch fish throughout the tournament. He utilized a 7-inch minnow on spinning tackle with varying head sizes as well as a 3/4-ounce football jig on the final day.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Pat Schlapper
programme.desc: Pat Schlapper recounts his finest tournament week to date where to took the title at the Sabine River. Schlapper relied on a few areas of the Sabine along with a few lures including a Do-It Molds compact jig he pours himself altering it with a smaller stouter hook. He also utilized a Brazalo Custom Lures Bushwhacker Buzz Bait in the morning on the final day when it put multiple quality fish in the boat.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes tackles where the fish go when they finish spawning but the water temperatures aren't at their hottest yet like they will be later in the summer. Cifuentes dives into three different baits that are useful around lakes with standing timber for the last week of May as we head into June.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Florida pro Bernie Schultz talks buzzbaits specifically two kinds. He keeps a squeaking buzzbait and clacking buzzbait ready to go at all times especially in the post-spawn. Although it's an excellent technique in the post-spawn Schultz acknowledges its use early in the year in places like Florida Texas and other southern states. Buzz it slow or fast make it clack or squeak add a toad or a trailer hook whatever you'd like with a buzzbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock explains a new bait he was introduced to that helps him catch not only deep northern smallmouth but also southern largemouth in the winter months. He also discusses the value in 2D sonar with this technique around structure in the south.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Roberston
programme.desc: Matt Robertson talks about upsizing his spinnerbait and adjusting his blade sizes when throwing this lure in water temperatures varying from the 40's to 50's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Austin Felix
programme.desc: Austin Felix gives his thoughts on when he picks up a Dropshot versus a Ned Rig and a Neko Rig. Speed is often the determining factor for each presentation and he tends to reserve the Neko for largemouth situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew talks about one of his favorite fun-fishing lures which is the Umbrella Rig aka Alabama Rig. LeHew utilizes this in multiple ways as he can cover water around shallow cover like he would with a spinnerbait but also with his electronics around deeper offshore structure.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New goes through some of the keys he likes in his jig when targeting bass in the prespawn. New breaks down his jig trailer and why it's efficient and also explains an adjustment to his jig size that he used to never use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher gives his take on a few productive lures in the prespawn and how he balances their uses to be most effective while on the water. Should you use a Chatterbait where a jig could also work or vice versa he attacks this and more in this scenario.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Card
programme.desc: Brandon Card gives his thoughts on early season jerkbait fishing. Card gives scenarios when he will opt for a different cadence for his jerkbait rod length and line size.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Cobb
programme.desc: Brandon Cobb gives his top picks for effective baits on lakes with blueback herring. Spotted bass and largemouth will get hyper focused on blueback herring when they exist on a body of water and Cobb knows these baits will work throughout the year and not a certain specific season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Taku Ito
programme.desc: Taku Ito goes through two key baits to his Bassmaster Elite Series victory at Smith Lake. From Neko Rigging a bluegill imitating bait to dropshotting a Magnum Fuzzy Dice he managed the biggest bass and bag to win.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Parks
programme.desc: Logan Parks discusses a strategy he employed at Wheeler during his first Top 10. Varying line size can help crankbaits run different depth and retrieved faster or slower. It's something he recommends during the summer months when schools are forming offshore or have been fished for frequently.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Latuso
programme.desc: Logan Latuso discusses a big key in the summer months...SHADE. This underrated aspect of the summer can get you some of the biggest bites of your day and it seemingly gets better as the day progresses. Take notes from Latuso and don't run your shade pattern too early to ensure some of your best success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Arey
programme.desc: Matt Arey talks about the importance of varying your retrieve with swimbaits over structure like brush piles. This is something that can be done with or without forward facing sonar as Arey describes the trial and error used prior to newer technology.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jake Whitaker
programme.desc: Jake Whitaker talks about the shallow bite windows that open up even with 100 degree days in the south. Whitaker leans on a topwater toad around any sort of cover that could hold fish. Anglers may get less bites in the heat of the summer but they can be the quality you need in a tournament.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Clifford Pirch
programme.desc: Clifford Pirch gives us a few ways to rig a drop shot if you're specifically targeting smallmouth and spotted bass. Threading his worm on weedless is his ideal setup but when fishing for smallmouth and spotted bass they tend to be more open water and less obstructions around. That's when Pirch will opt for a few other methods for fall rate and action.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Ed Laughran III
programme.desc: Lake Champlain Champion Ed Loughran runs through his jig setup that accounted for most of the fish throughout his tournament. He also leaned on a topwater in practice and on Championship Monday to catch smallmouth.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston gives a quick bait breakdown of a key lure that helped him win the 2024 Bassmaster Elite Series event at the St. Lawrence River. Johnston battled the waves out in Lake Ontario on the final two days of the event to secure a win his second of the season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jacob Foutz
programme.desc: Jacob Foutz walks us through his process of selecting sizes of jig heads when targeting bass in flooded timber. His sizes are as follows; 3/16 oz (5 to 10 feet) 1/4 oz (10 to 15 feet) 3/8 oz (20 feet and deeper). Foutz doesn't like getting any heavier than that if he can because of the leverage it gives fish to easily jump and throw the hook.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cody Huff
programme.desc: Cody Huff explores the benefits he's found when using various spoons during the late summer. He has dialed in his setups and doesn't experiment with multiple brands of spoons but rather uses the same spoons and changes sizes based on situation. From a magnum spoon to a compact jigging spoon Huff has found success on these from the Tennessee River to the Ozarks and many places in between.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey dishes out a few of his must-have baits for the early fall fishing season for Smallmouth bass. Downey who lives in Minnesota knows how incredible the bite can be this time of year before cold temps hit daily. Given the type of lake Downey has options for you in this video.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tyler Williams
programme.desc: Tyler Williams reveals the details to his 3/4 ounce jig he uses across the country. Upsizing his line can help slow the fall of his heavy jig along with pairing the jig with a big bulky trailer. Williams will use this jig around docks brush piles ledges and when targeting specific fish on his forward-facing sonar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: Greg Hackney gives some love to an often-forgotten lure for smallmouth fishing and that is the good ole fashioned tube. Hackney still appreciates what a tube brings to the table while fishing for smallmouth on competition days.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock talks about one of the most fun techniques and lures that is so effective in the Fall season. Covering water with a Berkley Choppo is essential and allows Shryock to burn through dead water in no time with this approach and it is a tournament winning formula.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt pulls 4 swim jigs out of his tackle box to showcase their effectiveness on different pieces of cover and depths. A simple trailer change can help Schmitt's swim jig stay shallow or go deeper. Schmitt gives the nuts and bolts to swim jig fishing his way and style.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Cox
programme.desc: John Cox gives a look at two of his favorite topwater lures and ones he trusts in the Fall. Whether it's around grass wood or rock both of these lures are on his front deck this time of year. Cox experimented with a longer frog rod this season and it helped him land a 3rd place finish at Wheeler Lake.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Lester
programme.desc: Brandon Lester gives us two key factors he relies on when choosing between a Jig and Texas Rig which is often a debate in the Fall fishing season. Profile and rate of fall depending on the seasonal conditions are considerations for the two-time BASS winner.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen runs down his three favorite colors for squarebill crankbaits in the fall. Another essential aspect to a squarebill that Lowen cherishes is a circuit board bill vs a plastic bill. It gives the crankbait the feel and characteristic of a balsa crankbait while maintaining the durability of a plastic crankbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Atkins
programme.desc: Justin Atkins sheds light on the flats. A vast area of consistent contour depths and also a place where baitfish and bass congregate as the season turns to cooler temperatures in the fall. This can be a great landing spot for bass as they get positioned to feed during this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson pulls out his favorite bait for the fall when the water temperatures are falling and in many situations the water level is falling too. When the bass start keying in on crawfish with cooling water J-Will knows its jig season. With living rubber skirted jigs Williamson fishes a 1/2 ounce or 3/4 ounce jig and never goes lighter than 1/2 ounce. He will also target brush early and as it continues to cool down will move to rock through the winter.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: One of the best structure fishermen in the world Brandon Palaniuk talks about isolated structure in the fall season. BP also gives a few bait suggestions including his handy dropshot.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin gives us his version of Thanksgiving turkey and fixings with this three-bait lineup this time of year. He has a bait for every level of the water column depending on how the fish are acting and where you're fishing this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes talks about the shallow nature of fish even when the temperatures are dropping across the country. The first feeling anglers have when the water temperatures drop is to fish deeper water but Cifuentes mentions how even in the Ozarks bass will hang out around shallow wood and rock still keyed in on a bigger meal that imitates dying baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Herren
programme.desc: Matt Herren goes through the process of fishing current seams on rivers with a spinnerbait. No matter time of year water current is a great place to find fish and target where bass are positioned and if you find the correct lineup it can be fast action. Herren recommends a 1/2-ounce to 3/4-ounce compact spinnerbait to avoid snags and hangups and control the bait despite the current pushing and washing the spinnerbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Alex Wetherell
programme.desc: Alex Wetherell discusses two soft plastics he uses around his home in Connecticut and down south when the calendar hits December. Balls of bait equal bass for Wetherell as they actively feed even when the water temperatures are cooler at the end of the year. Bass aren’t nearly as lethargic as we once believed years ago.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses fishing a jerkbait around Christmas time and how two of his baits act totally different. Christie breaks down how the Smithwick Rogue and Booyah Flash Point react different on the same cadence. Water temperatures in the 40's Christie opts for the Rogue. Meanwhile he sees positive results with the quick-working Flash Point with temperatures in the 50's and even 60's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Wes Logan
programme.desc: Wes Logan talks moving water and how he approaches it. Being from the Coosa River Logan is used to fishing moving water no matter the time of year and these three baits help him have good success.

programme.title: Truck U

programme.title: Truck U
programme.desc: When you start with a frame from a C-10 truck there is only one way for this project to go….down. We’ll give the C-10 frame a 2-inch drop and bolt on a ton of cool new parts.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The focus has shifted, with parts having arrived at the shop it’s time to install the Grill, Bumper, Dash and Interior of our 1968 Turbine Bronze Charger. Mark and the Ghouls work their magic on the Charger until a familiar face shows up. With Royal there, Mark shifts the crew back to the 1 of 2 1970 Coronet and finishes the interior. Then, it’s time for a test drive!

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: With SEMA 2018 looming on the horizon, it’s time to address the elephant in the room. Mark’s 1964 A100 Hemi truck, the Little Dead Wagon, built as an homage to Bill Maverick’s Little Red Wagon. Will is set to prime and paint, but has a disagreement with Mark over the color. When the engine for the A100 shows up it’s time to unbox one of the most powerful engines Graveyard Carz has ever put in a car!

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: Mark and the Ghouls get down to work like never before in order to get the A100 ready for SEMA which is only weeks away. Brakes, suspension, tail lights, bed sealer, you name it and the Mopar Maniacs are racing to get it done. With time flying and stress mounting the team works long hours and weekends trying to finish this iconic build. With SEMA only days away, the A100 finally gets it’s iconic 426 HEMI engine, well, if they can make it fit!

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: There is no time left, SEMA is almost here but the iconic A100 still needs some buttoning up. Installing all of the final components is an all hands on deck task and when the dust settles, Mark has only the decals left to put on the car, completing its legendary look. With the A100 finished the team heads out to SEMA in order to roll the Little Dead Wagon over the red carpet for Mopar and Mark once again receives a very kind gift from our friends.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: When Mark get’s started talking about a car there is almost no stopping him. So it is again when Mark picks multiple years of a favorite Mopar of his and tells both the audience, and whoever will listen all about their amazing options and cool differences. The Ghouls join in on the fun just like last time to pick their favorite things as well. Don’t worry, though, he can’t talk forever right?

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: With SEMA over the Ghoulz can finally rest and get back to work on all the cars they had to leave untouched for the last few weeks…again. First up on deck is our beautiful 1972 Duster. Needing its Dash installed as well as its interior there is still a lot of work left on this car! Additionally, metal work has begun on a host of new cars moving up through the shop, it never stops at Graveyard Carz.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: A 1970 Challenger is a special thing, but a B5 Challenger is even more special. With the bumblebee stripe finally added to the car it’s time for the work to really begin. Work begins on all the things that make this 1970 Challenger special, including the headliner, dash, interior and more. With that done it’s time for this beautiful Challenger to get its 440 Six Pack!

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The time has finally come. Brett Torino is coming and he is here for his car, the legendary 1 of 2 ever made, 1970 Coronet! Mark wouldn’t be Mark, though, without a few tricks up his sleeve. When Brett arrives to collect on his long restoration from the Mopar Master, the reveal of this truly one of a kind car is done with style. But not before Mark takes us back through the entire restoration leading up to that point. It Is the last 1970 Hemi Coronet Convertible on earth, after all.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The crew is overwhelmed with several restorations at once. From painting stripes, to engine parts, to missing parts on the 71 Charger, tensions are high around the shop. To Make things worse, Mark is obsessed with finding a factory pink Mopar for his granddaughter's 16th birthday.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The crew at Graveyard Carz are excited about the pumpkin carving contest, but when a mistake leaves the 'Cuda filled with water, the whole crew has to pay the price. Royal saves the day, but with the carving contest back on the table, where are the pumpkins? Mark has to swallow his pride and accept help from Daren for the contest to go ahead.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: Daren is given control of the shop for a week. Darenʼs constant pestering and ribbing leads Mark to hand him the reigns of Graveyard Carz for a week. But instead of getting things done, Daren starts inventing new field trips and distractions for the crew, as well as becoming obsessed with getting his personal Dodge Challenger running again.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: Mark receives an angry call from the owner of the 1970 Roadrunner, which leads to a mad rush to get the car finished in time. Meanwhile, Josh pushes the crew into committing to some New Years resolutions.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: Frustrated by the crew's complaints that he spends all day being lazy in the front office. Mark is determined to prove to the guys that there is more to restoring a car than physical labor. Josh and Daren visit the crash site of the mangled orange 1971 'Cuda.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: As the team works to complete a multitude of cars, Mark stresses over the metal dipping of the very rare and valuable ʻ71 Cuda 440-6. Tensions are high and time is limited, is the GYC crew up to the pressure?

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The ghouls get the remains back from the '71 440 Six Barrel, 4 Speed, Shaker Hood Phantom Cuda and determine if the car can be resurrected. A '69 Dodge Daytona Charger arrives ready to be brought back from the dead and Mark gets a 2011 SRT8 Dodge Challenger.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The ghouls get the N96 Air Grabber installed on the '71 Charger 440 Six Pack Triple Green car. It's started and is ready for final assembly. The owners of '70 Cuda 383 Automatic FE5 Rallye Red Car visit to check on the restoration progress.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: Mark is hired to restore the body, paint, and suspension of a '70 AAR Cuda 340 Six Barrel car. The shop gets some needed upgrades and the '71 Charger 440 Six Pack Triple Green car is completed to OEM Specifications.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The '70 Sunroof Challenger is painted and ready for final assembly. The '69 Daytona Charger is disassembled and readied to be shipped to the media blasters. Mark and the Ghoulz head out to the junkyard to blow off some steam playing paintball.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: Mark and the Ghoulz use their brand new Shop Crane to lower the body of the '71 Cuda 340 Triple Black 'Phantasm' Tribute car onto its restored suspension and its drive-train is assembled and installed.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The '69 Daytona Charger returns from the media blaster and Mark gives Josh a history lesson on the '70 AAR Cuda 340 Six Barrel Car before removing it's drive-train and suspension.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The ghouls get the '70 AAR Cuda 340 Six Barrel car completely disassembled and off to the media blaster. Mark disassembles and restores the right-hand door to the 71' 440 Phantom Cuda. In addition, the headliner and vinyl top is installed in the 71 'Phantasm' Tribute car.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The ghouls get the '70 AAR Cuda 340 Six Barrel car completely disassembled and off to the media blaster. Mark disassembles and restores the right-hand door to the 71' 440 Phantom Cuda. In addition, the headliner and vinyl top is installed in the 71 'Phantasm' Tribute car.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The owner of the '70 AAR Cuda 340 Six Barrel car visits the shop and learns about assembly-line markings. Mark checks the paint on the body of the '70 Cuda 383 Automatic FE5 Rallye Red Car and discovers a major problem.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The ghouls receives a '70 Barracuda Convertible to get a full restoration. Despite improbability, Mark straightens the fender for the '71 440 Phantom Cuda and the crew continues the restoration of the '71 'Phantasm' Tribute car.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The ghouls receives a '70 Barracuda Convertible to get a full restoration. Despite improbability, Mark straightens the fender for the '71 440 Phantom Cuda and the crew continues the restoration of the '71 'Phantasm' Tribute car.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The ghouls detail and assemble the suspension of the '70 AAR Cuda 340 Six Barrel car. The owners of the '70 Plymouth Superbird, in the queue for resurrection, visit the shop and Daren convinces the crew to throw a birthday party for Mark.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: Mark takes some time for himself and leaves Daren in charge of the shop. The crew gets the newly painted panels installed on the '70 Cuda 383 Automatic FE5 Rallye Red Car. And Mark discovers a chip on the '71 'Phantasm' Tribute car and no one will own up to it.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The fuel and brake lines are installed in the '71 'Phantasm' Tribute car. Daren quits and won't return until Mark begins the restoration of his '70 Plum Crazy Challenger. A phone-call from the Phantasm car owner forces Mark to make a promise he might not be able to keep.

programme.title: Graveyard Carz
programme.desc: The GYC crew is under the gun to get the '71 Cuda 340 Triple Black 'Phantasm' Tribute car finished by the end of the week. With the exhaust, ornamation, and the engine start still ahead of them, will they be able to finish the car before the director of the 'Phantasm' movie franchise arrives?

programme.title: What's In the Barn?
programme.desc: An family farm in the mid-west contains houses, barns, outbuildings, trailers, grain silos and buses full of old stuff and perhaps the biggest stash of undiscovered old motorcycles in the country. The collection was put together by their unnamed father. Seller agrees to have Dale broker rare Excelsior for high-end client. Dale has the buyer, but will he outbid his own client for the exclusive find?

programme.title: What's In the Barn?
programme.desc: Matt is out for revenge. Last year Dale beat him badly at the Annual Vintage bike race in Barber, Alabama. But this year there is a whole new tale to tell. With just days until the race - Dale is secretly struggling to get the bike he beat Matt with last year up and working. Matt struggles just to locate a 100-year old bike. Matt's prayers are answered thanks to an old Catholic Priest he located who has possession of a bike. The priest might let Matt have the bike to race - but there are conditions. The toughest one: Don't tell Dale you have it. Can Matt afford to buy the bike and get it running in time for the race without Dale seeing it? Will Dale even get his broken bike started? And if they ever get to race, will Matt exact his revenge?

programme.title: What's In the Barn?
programme.desc: Built in the mid-60’s by eccentric engineer “Wild Bill” Gelbke, the Road Dog was, and still is, the largest motorcycle ever built. It utilized aircraft tubing, Corvette disc brakes, and a Chevy truck differential to keep it stable. The one-off creation disappeared when Gelbke did in 1978. Outflanked once when the bike was spotted and sold to a private collector in 1995, Dale has vowed to locate the machine and make Wheels Through Time its final resting place.

programme.title: What's In the Barn?

programme.title: What's In the Barn?
programme.desc: For Dale and Matt sometimes the dotted line to treasure splits and heads in opposite directions. In this edition of What’s in the Barn, time is thrust to the forefront of this multi-state, long distance, north, south search. programme.title: Earth from above - Season 4 - Nature’s Heroes: Bangladesh - Part 1
programme.desc: With Bangladesh as a running thread, Yann Arthus-Bertrand meets several people who have changed their lives to dedicate themselves to a major project. In Bangladesh, Yves and Runa Marre have created the Friendship Foundation. Among other things, they’ve created a floating hospital installed on an old barge bought in France. Julie Andersen, an ex-advertising executive from New York has come to South Africa to defend sharks with her Shark Angels Foundation. In North India, Kartik Satyanarayan is helping to stop the dreadful exploitation of the lippus bears (dancing bears). He’s created Wildlife SOS, a preserve to rehabilitate the bears that have been rescued and to give work to the men of the tribe who were traditionally bear tamers and entertainers.

programme.title: Earth from above - Season 3 - USA: The end of oil - Part 1
programme.desc: "The end of oil" is the amazing story of a raw material which has revolutionized man's life in just a century. But today, oil reserves are depleting. In his crazy race for always more production, Man didn't manage to preserve this precious energy that took million years for the Earth to give out. To tell the adventure of oil, Yann Arthus-Bertrand and his team went to the United States, the country which depends the most on black gold. At the start of the 21st century, it is now urgent to realize that oil resources are limited. It's today that we have to act and get organized, in order to prepare the new era to come. While all our economies are based on the petrol barrel's price, we'll have to learn to do without oil within 20, 30 or 100 years. What will be the consequences? What are the solutions at stake? This new episode of Earth From Above attempts to answer these questions. From China to Benin, including Azerbaijan, Belgium and Canada, Earth From Above takes us on a new trip around the world, in search of black gold.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook - Season 4 - A la carte grills
programme.desc: If you're a nature enthusiast and a fan of outdoor cooking, the upcoming season is perfect for barbecue enthusiasts! Our journey will take us to Aube, nestled in the heart of the Brévonnes forest, and then to the Massif des Bauges, where grilling and snow create a unique combination. Afterward, we'll explore the Libournais region, where we'll uncover cooking techniques that make use of vine shoots, which are plentiful in the area. Just a short distance from the vineyards, we'll arrive at another corner of Gironde, the Blaye region, where the cooking method remains consistent but features a distinctly local ingredient: eel.

programme.title: My Zen People - Season 3 - Hansen
programme.desc: A former model and Sports News anchor, Hansen has drifted away from the limelight to focus on a personal journey. His Yoga trip began 10 years ago, after suffering a herniated disc injury. His experiences have taught him that the only way one can truly change the world is to raise the consciousness of humanity, and this actually starts within ourselves.

programme.title: My Zen People - Season 3 - Mark, Camille & Juliana
programme.desc: A Filipino couple with a shared love for traveling decide to change their lives and explore a passion for eco-tourism. Their glamping tents are perched on the hills of Bacuit Bay and promise a natural and enriching experience. Daily sunset yoga sessions and Farm-to-Table dining are just some of the activities they share with their guests. Their energy attracts like-minded people on similar journeys, notably their yoga teacher Juliana who has an inspiring story of her own to share with us.

programme.title: My Zen Family - Season 1 - Last preps
programme.desc: Clara and Gianni’s boys are born! But they came in a little bit early, and have been admitted in neonatal resuscitation... Coralie and Florent are still walking on clouds as they wait for their daughter, Lena. So are Nathalie and Naoufel, who arrange a tour of the future baby’s bedroom. Things are still tense between Kim and her parents. Her father blames here for having left school too early and the family makes no effort to hide their dislike of Pierre, the would-be father, who is still a no-show. They go as far as opposing Kim’s preferred choice for the future boy’s name, since it was his father that came up with the idea...

programme.title: My Zen Family - Season 1 - Welcome in a new world
programme.desc: All the babies are born! How are Clara and Gianni coping with the situation with two newborn children at home? Does this help them to mourn the loss of their unborn second baby? Was Coralie allowed her much-desired epidural? Did Pierre came back at Kim’s side to finally act as the father, and what name did Kim settle upon for her son? In the end, it is Nathalie and Naoufel, our most experienced parents, who share with us some words of wisdom: “one isn’t just born being a parent, one has to learn it.”

programme.title: Reset - Season 1 - Greece, Euphoria Retreat
programme.desc: In this episode of Reset, embark on a transformative journey to Euphoria Retreat. - A mystical place offering a holistic approach to well-being aimed at restoring balance between body, mind and soul. - After a long struggle with illness, its founder embarked on a personal quest to find balance. An in-depth reflection which resulted in the creation of a place where one could share and transmit this method of well-being. Euphoria Retreat is a clever blend of Taoist and Hellenic philosophy based on the symbolism of the five elements: water, wood, fire, earth and metal. Ancestral wisdom and scientific advances offer a transformative immersion in self-discovery. The tools developed by Euphoria Retreat allow everyone to become their own healer.

programme.title: Reset - Season 1 - Italy, Palazzo Fiuggi
programme.desc: In this episode of Reset we discover Palazzo Fiuggi, a haven of well-being located in the heart of the natural springs of Fiuggi, famous for their purifying and healing powers. - The Palazzo was born from the vision of a science and health enthusiast. This historic place of well-being offers exclusive medical-scientific therapies combining the healing properties of water with advances in Western medicine and alternative medicines. Upon arrival, a team of specialists carries out a targeted diagnosis to create a personalized protocol, rebalancing the mind, body and soul, with a simple promise: offering a longer and better-lived life. - A constantly evolving method, between ancestral wisdom and innovation, where the Palazzo Fiuggi medical spa presents an avant-garde wellness experience, integrating cutting-edge technologies to understand and analyze individual needs, but also to support physical regeneration. This integrative approach goes beyond the simple treatment of symptoms, seeking to heal the body, mind and soul as a whole, thus elevating the concept of spa treatment to a new level.

Her love for dance and desire for movement drove her to quit her corporate life and begin a new chapter as a fitness trainer. Quickly exhausting the traditional methods available at her local gyms, she began to create innovative and groundbreaking exercise methods of her own. Her goal: to empower women by making them feel strong and feminine at the same time.

programme.title: Earth from above - Season 2 - So the great rivers may live - Part 1
programme.desc: Water and its beauty, water and its power, water and its fragility... the water we all need is becoming scarce, through our own fault. Some rivers are dry, others are diverted, cut off by dams, others are simply polluted, and this for decades. We will discover how humans transformed the nature in Argentina, then in China and its disproportionate Three Gorges Dam. We will also go in Botswana with the Okavango, this unique river which flows into a desert forming the famous Okavango Delta. Vu du Ciel makes you discover once again another world, magnificent but threatened.

programme.title: Reset - Season 1 - France, Le Bruit de l'eau
programme.desc: In this episode of Reset, we take you to “Le Bruit de l'eau”, an ecolodge nestled in the heart of the Baie de Somme nature reserve, in France. In the middle of nature, discover a place of absolute serenity inspired by the Japanese lifestyle and the travels of a great reporter, its founder. - The intimate atmosphere that reigns at Le Bruit de l'eau (The Sound of Water) envelops you in a soothing calm, creating a cocoon made for relaxation and personal rejuvenation. - This ecolodge allows us to cultivate awareness of the present moment and to open up to a fulfilling perception of our environment. Le Bruit de l'eau opens the doors to a transformative experience, where beauty of the natural environment merges with quest for serenity.

programme.title: Reset - Season 1 - Sri Lanka, Santani
programme.desc: In this episode of Reset, we fly to Sri Lanka to discover an old tea plantation transformed into a sumptuous refuge: Santani. - In order to find an alternative to the stress of urban life, the hotel offers a modern approach to Ayurveda. This traditional Indian medicine aims to establish a balance between the individual and the world around them. Thanks to the development of a personalized program, each visitor is invited to find harmony within this restorative sanctuary. - Santani was created by a Sri Lankan eager to preserve our physical and spiritual well-being in a peaceful and healthy place to reconnect with the world differently. Let's discover a holistic approach to health, including Ayurvedic medicine and the ancient practices of yoga and meditation. Santani opens the doors to a world of tranquility.

programme.title: My Day Dubai - Season 1 - Atlantis
programme.desc: In this episode, our presenter Gabriela will visit Sustainable City in Dubai. She will discover how the residents garden, how they dress in sustainable clothes and, of course, how they eat by preparing healthy recipes. She will end her day with a Qigong class with a Qigong master.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook - Season 4 - The flavors of chocolate
programme.desc: Today, the gluttons should not be disappointed since chocolate is in the spotlight. Discovered by the Mayans 2500 years ago and then more widely by the Aztecs, chocolate is today one of the favorite products in the world. And make no mistake about it: just as the kitchen has its great chefs, chocolate also has its great chocolatiers. - As for recipes, Julie will introduce you to a cake that is only made in Saint Émilien and which combines chocolate with macarons, before heading to the Basque Country for a dessert to spice you up. We will then climb up the mountain to meet a Swiss cook. Finally, you will see that chocolate has several surprises in store for us: it has many virtues and is also used for well-being.

programme.title: My Zen People - Season 4 - Agostina (Argentina)
programme.desc: When Agostina’s mother was diagnosed with breast cancer, she began seeking out soft natural fabrics that would not irritate her mother’s sensitive skin. She found it almost impossible to find the right materials, so she decided to make her own. Research led her to bamboo fibers and she realised she could make a positive impact on the environment, while developing sustainable and ethical fashion.

programme.title: My Zen People - Season 4 - Solenn (Nantes)
programme.desc: A former school teacher reinvents herself when she discovers a passion for sharing other women’s stories. Always inspired by the journeys of strong women, Solenn began a blog to celebrate the women in her community. - Solenn’s energy and passion fueled a dream of starting her own magazine. Thanks to a successful crowdfunding campaign, this dream blossomed into a professional career in journalism and she launched a print mook (magazine & book) called Etonnantes. Etonnantes features interviews of women of all backgrounds, celebrating their diversity and success in each field.

programme.title: My Zen People - Season 4 - Sophie (Nantes)
programme.desc: Always an artist at heart, Sophie grew up in the countryside amongst nature and farm animals. Her love for creating art while respecting nature turned into a drive to seek out sustainable vegetable dyes. - Today, her artwork and craft are intertwined as she makes beautiful prints and motifs that she colours with natural dyes, prepared from handpicked variety of flowers and plants that turn into stunning creations.

programme.title: Earth from above - Season 2 - So the great rivers may live - Part 2
programme.desc: Yann Arthus-Bertrand thus continues his world tour and his inventory of the planet with the great rivers that suffer from man's excesses as a common thread. " So the great rivers may live" is the discovery of places, men and women who are fighting so that our waterways simply have their place on Earth. Thanks to his genius, man is correcting his mistakes: the Aral Sea, which once disappeared, is coming back. In New York, millions of people have drinking water thanks to the natural virtues of the forest.

programme.title: Earth from above - Season 2 - Of Forests and Men - Part 2
programme.desc: The call of the Forest is about discovering places but above all it is about meeting those who protect this priceless heritage. Forests are essential to mankind. They capture CO2, promote the formation of clouds and therefore rain, protect the soil from erosion and provide a habitat for wildlife. From Madagascar, to France, to Cameroon, or even Eritrea, Yann Arthus-Bertrand sets out to discover the most beautiful forests, those who live in them, those who protect them and those who live off them.

programme.title: Julie's Frenchy Cookbook - Season 4 - The cheese menu
programme.desc: Today, Julie sets on the roads of France to talk about an essential product on French tables: cheese. More than a gourmet craze, more than an end-of-meal treat, cheese is associated with French gastronomy, and is also recognized as Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO. With nearly 1,000 varieties (soft cheeses, cooked, blue-veined, pressed cheeses…), the French are the biggest consumers of cheese in the world!

programme.title: Breaking Pickleball

programme.title: National Collegiate Pickleball Association (NCPA)
programme.desc: Experience the pinnacle of collegiate pickleball as Virginia Tech and Liberty University battle for the NCPA 2025 Virginia Beach Regional title. This high-stakes championship matchup features a prize pool of $2,500 and a chance for regional dominance.The action kicks off with an elite men’s doubles match featuring Liberty’s Ben Rice and Derek Cray against Virginia Tech’s undefeated Cody Miller and Caelan Funk. The broadcast also captures intense singles play and critical mixed doubles rallies as both teams fight through high-tension dink battles and "Dreambreaker" level strategy. Watch for standout defensive plays, including ATP (Around the Post) attempts and high-speed hand battles on the Championship Court at Pickleball Virginia Beach.

programme.title: World Pickleball League (WPBL)
programme.desc: Experience the high-octane energy of the World Pickleball League (WPBL) Season 2 as the Bengaluru Jawans go head-to-head with the Rajasthan Titans at the iconic Jio World Garden in Mumbai. The stakes are higher than ever in this Day 9, Tie 16 clash, featuring elite matchups such as the "women's singles player of the season" Katrina Stewart facing off against the resilient Lorena Dupnik. Watch as tactical masters like Dusty Boyer and Jack Foster battle for supremacy in a series of intense singles and mixed doubles competitions where every point counts toward the league standings. With game-changing "Pickle Plays" and atmospheric "drums" fueling the intensity, this tie is a masterclass in professional grit and strategic precision.

programme.title: All Florida Pro League
programme.desc: Commentators provide an inside look at Game 2 of the All Florida Pro League (AFPL) Stop 4 in Sarasota, Florida. The Fort Myers Flamingos get off to a dominant start, but the Jacksonville Ballers refuse to give up, staging a dramatic late-game comeback that tightens the score and mounts the pressure. This episode features key players like Stevie, Sophia Dorsey, and Maddalena, with highlights of their strategic plays and powerful shots. Tune in to see if the Flamingos can hold on to their lead and close out the game against the surging Ballers.

programme.title: NPL
programme.desc: The Indianapolis Drivers take on the Princeton Bruisers in a mixed team match.

programme.title: NPL
programme.desc: The Coachella Valley Scorpions take on the Denver Iconics in a thrilling women’s National Pickleball League showdown from the 2024 season. From powerful baseline drives to lightning-fast net battles, both teams bring competitive spirit and polished teamwork to the court. Whether you're a seasoned fan or new to the NPL, this match showcases the rising talent and intensity of women’s pro pickleball. Every point matters — and momentum can shift in a flash.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2023
programme.desc: Parris Todd and Simone Jardim compete with Bobbi Oshiro and Megan Fudge for gold in this Gold Medal Match.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2025
programme.desc: Get ready for an exciting Mixed Split Pro Age pickleball match featuring the formidable team of Jaime Oncins and Simone Jardim against the new pairing of Ryan Miscik and Christie Domoracki. Oncins is a former professional tennis player from Brazil. His partner, Simone Jardim, is a professional pickleball player, a Pickleball Hall of Fame inductee, and was once ranked the number one female player in the world. They face a new team with Ryan Miscik, a pro pickleball player and coach based in Venice, Florida. His partner, Christie Domoracki, is a player located in Boca Grande, Florida. This match brings together a mix of experienced pros and up-and-coming talent for a high-stakes competition on Florida's Paradise Coast.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2023
programme.desc: Parris Todd and Simone Jardim battles against Alix Truong and Milan Rane in the Women's Pro Doubles Semifinal match.

programme.title: European Pickleball Championship
programme.desc: Witness one of the most exciting finals from the European Pickleball Championships 2025 in Rome. In the Women's Senior Singles Open Final, Team England’s Anna Linton takes on Team Italy’s Paola Tampieri at the iconic Stadio dei Marmi. Linton starts with commanding form, dominating the first game with powerful forehand drives. However, the momentum shifts as Tampieri, fueled by a passionate home crowd, adjusts her strategy to target Linton’s backhand and level the match.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2025
programme.desc: Get ready for a great singles match as Simone Jardim takes on Kristen Kopp at the Usopp National Pickleball Center. This venue, home to the Usopp Pickleball Academy, is a hub for lessons and training, making it an amazing facility for all things pickleball.

programme.desc: Pickleball star Ryan Sherry & former NFL linebacker Brandon Siler vs. pickleball star Lew Halski & former NFL linebacker David Pollack.

programme.desc: Megan Fudge and Karin Kochis take on Ryann Foster and Lee Whitwell in this Women's Split Pro Doubles semifinal match.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2024
programme.desc: David Weinbach and Altaf Merchant take on Dayne Gingrich and Mircea Morariu in this Men's Senior Pro Doubles Gold Medal Match.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2025
programme.desc: Witness an unexpected and electrifying Mixed Pro Doubles showdown from the Minto US Open Pickleball Championships in Naples, Florida! Originally scheduled for a back court, this highly anticipated match featuring Andre Agassi and Anna Leigh Waters was moved to Championship Court due to overwhelming crowd demand, creating an unforgettable atmosphere. Relive every moment as these top players battle it out in a thrilling display of professional pickleball. Don't miss the action from East Naples Community Park – the epicenter of pickleball!

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2025
programme.desc: Get ready for thrilling Pro Men's Doubles pickleball action from the Minto US Open Pickleball Championships at East Naples Community Park, the National Pickleball Center! This semi-final match features the dynamic duo of Richard Livornese Jr. and Ryler Deheart against the formidable team of Ben Newell and Brandon Lane. Witness incredible rallies, aggressive plays, and strategic dinks as these top players battle it out for a spot in Championship Saturday. Don't miss this high-energy competition from the epicenter of pickleball!

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2023
programme.desc: Don’t miss this inspiring wheelchair hybrid doubles match from the 2023 US Open Pickleball Championships. Adaptive athletes Rob Krizmanich, Michael Lipp, Patick Huletsky, and Jeff Sylvestre bring talent, teamwork, and tenacity to the court in a showcase of the sport’s inclusive future.

programme.title: World Pickleball League (WPBL)
programme.desc: Experience the electric atmosphere of the World Pickleball League (WPBL) Season 2 as the Mumbai Pickle Power face off against the Bengaluru Jawans in a high-stakes Tie 9. With Mumbai hunting for their first outright victory and Bengaluru desperate to bounce back from a recent loss, the pressure at the Jio World Garden is at an all-time high. Watch as elite players like the "unstoppable" Katrina Stewart dominate the court in singles, while Brandon Lane and Glaura Carvajal Lane attempt to turn the tide for Mumbai in a masterclass of tactical doubles. This tie features the league’s most innovative strategies, from high-risk Pickle Plays to the pursuit of the prestigious Band of Honor, ensuring every rally is a battle for survival on the road to the semi-finals.

programme.title: World Pickleball League (WPBL)
programme.desc: Step into the electric Jio World Garden in Mumbai for a high-stakes showdown where the road to the playoffs is on the line. Delhi Dilwale enter this tie in second place, looking to solidify their dominance and secure a "Q" next to their name for a guaranteed spot in the semifinals. On the other side, Pune United are fighting for survival, desperately needing a win after finally breaking their season-long drought earlier in the day. Witness intense matchups as tactical veterans like Trang Huynh and Max Mansoor face off against Pune's resilient stars, including the grit of Katie Morris and the power of William Sobeck. In a league where every rally counts toward the "Band of Honor," these athletes must battle both their opponents and the relentless 15-minute clock in a masterclass of professional pickleball.

programme.title: US Open Pickleball Championships 2023
programme.desc: Watch a masterclass in senior pro pickleball as Peter Prodanov and Scott Moore take on Scott Crandall and Jose Derisi. With explosive hands, strategic play, and experience driving every point, this US Open quarterfinal is a showcase of skill, grit, and high-level doubles tactics.

programme.title: All Florida Pro League
programme.desc: This episode features courtside commentary on a ladies doubles match between the Sarasota Manatees and the GNV Chomp, followed by a men's doubles match between the same two teams. The ladies match showcases the absolute dominance of the top-seeded GNV Chomp, with players like Heather Nobler and Kelsey Laurent proving why they're a force to be reckoned with. The Sarasota Manatees, with new player Andy Godwin, fight to improve their league standing. The episode then transitions to a close men's doubles match featuring players Tobias Moreno and BK for the Chomp and Jamir and Jared Brooks for the Manatees.

programme.title: Picklebowl 2022
programme.desc: Watch as Pickleball Pros Dan Granot and Phillip Phillips, paired with NFL legend Brandon Siler and Pickleball professional Ryan Sherry, battle it out in this thrilling Men's Doubles match from the Picklebowl 2022. Filmed in the stunning Sea Island, Georgia, this unique event brings together celebrities and professional athletes representing their alma maters. The game is not only about competition but also raising funds for a great cause, benefiting Desire Street Ministries. With star power from both the sports and entertainment worlds, this exciting match is filled with hard-hitting shots, strategic play, and thrilling moments that will keep you on the edge of your seat.

programme.title: Pickleball England
programme.desc: Experience the exciting Women's Doubles Open 4.5+ Final from the 2023 English Open held at Bolton Arena, Greater Manchester. This match features dynamic teams: Megan Fudge and Susannah Barr face off against Lee Whitwell and Riley Bohnert in a highly competitive final. Follow expert commentary highlighting key plays including Susannah Barr’s precise lobs, Megan Fudge’s powerful forehand, and strategic teamwork. See how the match unfolds in a best-of-three games format with a hard stop on time. This showcase of top-level English pickleball captures the skill, tactics, and intensity of the sport. Stay tuned for post-match insights and upcoming mixed doubles action.

programme.title: The Wager
programme.desc: Set at the scenic Troubadour Golf and Field Club in Nashville, TN, this exhibition match brings a mix of celebrity flair and friendly competition to the pickleball court. Olympian Shawn Johnson and her husband Andrew East take on TV host Jason Kennedy and pro Wes Burrows in a lighthearted yet tightly contested match that goes down to the wire. With Shawn still learning the ropes (and the rules), and Andrew channeling his athletic instincts, the duo puts up an impressive fight against the more experienced Kennedy and Burrows. It’s a fast-paced, fun-filled match full of laughs, learning moments, and great rallies—perfect for fans of lifestyle sports and celebrity matchups.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik takes Professor Von Schlemmer hostage and uses his growth machine to try and enlarge himself.
